--[[
	The colour over life (ColorSequence) editor: holds the stops and the operations both bodies call.
	Outside Classic the body is ViewStops (a strip with pins, the colour wheel inline, the effect's
	colours, Reverse / Even spacing / Smooth hues). Classic's body (BuildUI) works like Roblox's own
	ColorSequence editor: triangles under the bar, a click on the bar adds a stop, a click on the
	selected stop opens the ColorPicker, the end stops stay put.
	  new(screenGui, theme, colorPicker, settings)
	  Open(colorSequence, propertyName, onApply, onPreview, position, options), Close(), IsOpen(),
	  GetPanel(), RefreshTheme(), Destroy(), IsPlacedByHand(), SetPlacedByHand(), ResizesByHand()
]]

local buildUI = require(script.BuildUI)
local ViewStops = require(script.ViewStops)
local UIConstants = require(script.Parent.UIBuilder.Constants)
local TypeScale = require(script.Parent.UIBuilder.TypeScale)
local SequenceClipboard = require(script.Parent.SequenceClipboard)

local ColorGradientEditor = {}
ColorGradientEditor.__index = ColorGradientEditor
-- ColorSequence.new throws above this many keypoints.
ColorGradientEditor.MOST_STOPS = 20

local PANEL_W = 280
local PANEL_H = 160
local BAR_H = 30
local BAR_SLICES = 64
local STOP_W = 10
local STOP_H = 12

-- ColorSequence has no Sample(t): walk the keypoints and lerp.
local function sampleColorSequence(cs, t)
	local kps = cs.Keypoints
	if t <= kps[1].Time then return kps[1].Value end
	if t >= kps[#kps].Time then return kps[#kps].Value end
	for i = 1, #kps - 1 do
		if t >= kps[i].Time and t <= kps[i+1].Time then
			local alpha = (t - kps[i].Time) / (kps[i+1].Time - kps[i].Time)
			return kps[i].Value:Lerp(kps[i+1].Value, alpha)
		end
	end
	return kps[#kps].Value
end

-- A ColorSequence from the stops, sorted on a copy (the end-stop locks go by index); a single stop
-- becomes two keypoints.
local function stopsToColorSequence(stops)
	local copy = table.create(#stops)
	for i, s in ipairs(stops) do copy[i] = s end
	table.sort(copy, function(a, b) return a.time < b.time end)
	local kps = {}
	for _, s in ipairs(copy) do
		table.insert(kps, ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(math.clamp(s.time, 0, 1), s.color))
	end
	if #kps < 2 then
		kps = {ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(0, Color3.new(1,1,1)), ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(1, Color3.new(1,1,1))}
	end
	return ColorSequence.new(kps)
end

-- settings (the plugin) keeps the stops view's saved presets; without it they last the session.
function ColorGradientEditor.new(screenGui, theme, colorPicker, settings)
	local self = setmetatable({}, ColorGradientEditor)
	self._T = theme
	self._screenGui = screenGui
	self._settings = settings
	self._colorPicker = colorPicker
	self._conns = {}
	self._stopsToCS = stopsToColorSequence
	self._stops = {} -- {time, color}
	self._selectedIndex = nil
	self._originalCS = nil
	self._closing = false
	self._dragging = false
	self._dragIndex = nil
	self._pickerOpen = false
	self._pickerPreColor = nil -- colour before the picker opened, for Cancel
	-- Set by a drag of the panel (BuildUI) and by Modules/PanelPersistence restoring a saved place.
	self._placedByHand = false

	self._state = {
		propName = "",
		onApply = nil,
		onPreview = nil,
	}

	-- Outside Classic the stops view, where its wheel can be drawn; else Classic's body.
	if not UIConstants.MODE.Structure.Classic then
		self._view = ViewStops.build(self)
	end
	if self._view then
		self._panel = self._view.panel
	else
		buildUI(self, PANEL_W, PANEL_H, BAR_H, BAR_SLICES, STOP_W, STOP_H)
	end
	return self
end

function ColorGradientEditor:_renderBar()
	local cs = stopsToColorSequence(self._stops)
	for i = 1, BAR_SLICES do
		local t = (i - 0.5) / BAR_SLICES
		self._barSlices[i].BackgroundColor3 = sampleColorSequence(cs, t)
	end
end

function ColorGradientEditor:_renderStops()
	local T = self._T
	-- Grows the frame pool to #_stops. Frame i always shows the i-th stop in time (the stops stay
	-- sorted), so capturedIdx is a slot, not a stop.
	while #self._stopFrames < #self._stops do
		local idx = #self._stopFrames + 1
		local sf = Instance.new("TextLabel"); sf.Name = "Stop"..idx
		sf.BackgroundTransparency = 1; sf.Text = "\u{25B2}"; sf.Font = Enum.Font.GothamBold; sf.TextSize = 14
		sf.Size = UDim2.new(0, STOP_W, 0, STOP_H); sf.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0)
		sf.ZIndex = 6; sf.Parent = self._stopArea
		-- A TextLabel has no Activated: an invisible button 2 px larger on each side takes the click.
		local btn = Instance.new("TextButton"); btn.Name = "Click"; btn.BackgroundTransparency = 1
		btn.Text = ""; btn.Size = UDim2.new(1,4,1,4); btn.Position = UDim2.new(0,-2,0,-2)
		btn.ZIndex = 7; btn.Parent = sf
		local capturedIdx = idx
		btn.Activated:Connect(function()
			self:_onStopClick(capturedIdx)
		end)
		table.insert(self._stopFrames, {frame = sf, btn = btn})
	end
	for i, stop in ipairs(self._stops) do
		local sf = self._stopFrames[i]
		sf.frame.Visible = true
		sf.frame.Position = UDim2.new(stop.time, 0, 0, 0)
		local isSelected = (i == self._selectedIndex)
		sf.frame.TextColor3 = isSelected and T.BrightGold or stop.color
	end
	for i = #self._stops + 1, #self._stopFrames do
		self._stopFrames[i].frame.Visible = false
	end
	if self._selectedIndex and self._stops[self._selectedIndex] then
		local s = self._stops[self._selectedIndex]
		self._timeInput.Text = string.format("%.2f", s.time)
		self._deleteBtn.TextColor3 = (#self._stops > 2 and self._selectedIndex > 1 and self._selectedIndex < #self._stops) and T.Red or T.DarkGold
	else
		self._timeInput.Text = "-"
	end
end

function ColorGradientEditor:_render()
	if self._view then
		self._view.render()
		return
	end
	self:_renderBar()
	self:_renderStops()
end

-- Shows stops that were just loaded and makes every one of them draggable.
function ColorGradientEditor:_showLoaded()
	self:_render()
	for index = 1, #self._stops do
		if self._stopDragWirer then self._stopDragWirer(index) end
	end
end

function ColorGradientEditor:_firePreview()
	if self._state.onPreview then
		self._state.onPreview(stopsToColorSequence(self._stops))
	end
end

-- What the Copy button does: the gradient as it stands goes to the shared sequence clipboard.
function ColorGradientEditor:_copy()
	SequenceClipboard.set(stopsToColorSequence(self._stops))
end

-- What the Paste button does: the clipboard's ColorSequence replaces the stops. Returns false
-- when the clipboard holds none.
function ColorGradientEditor:_paste()
	local sequence = SequenceClipboard.get("ColorSequence")
	if not sequence then
		return false
	end
	self:_load(sequence)
	return true
end

-- A whole sequence in place of the stops (Paste, a preset), drawn and previewed.
function ColorGradientEditor:_load(sequence)
	self:_loadCS(sequence)
	self:_showLoaded()
	self:_firePreview()
end

-- Apply: the gradient goes to whoever opened the editor, which closes without Cancel's revert.
function ColorGradientEditor:_apply()
	if self._state.onApply then
		self._state.onApply(stopsToColorSequence(self._stops))
	end
	self._originalCS = nil
	self:_rawClose()
end

function ColorGradientEditor:_onStopClick(index)
	-- A stale click from a frame whose stop was deleted.
	if index > #self._stops then return end
	-- Set by BuildUI's InputEnded when the press moved: the drag wins over the click.
	if self._wasDrag then self._wasDrag = false; return end
	if self._selectedIndex == index then
		-- A click on the selected stop opens the picker.
		self:_openPickerForStop(index)
	else
		self._selectedIndex = index
		self:_renderStops()
	end
end

function ColorGradientEditor:_openPickerForStop(index)
	local picker = self._colorPicker
	if not picker then return end
	local stop = self._stops[index]
	if not stop then return end

	self._pickerOpen = true
	self._pickerPreColor = stop.color

	picker:SetOnColorChanged(function(newColor)
		if self._stops[index] then
			self._stops[index].color = newColor
			self:_render()
			self:_firePreview()
		end
	end)

	picker:SetOnOK(function()
		self._pickerOpen = false
	end)

	picker:SetOnCancel(function()
		if self._stops[index] and self._pickerPreColor then
			self._stops[index].color = self._pickerPreColor
			self:_render()
			self:_firePreview()
		end
		self._pickerOpen = false
	end)

	picker:Open(stop.color, "Stop Color")
end

function ColorGradientEditor:_addStopAt(time)
	if #self._stops >= ColorGradientEditor.MOST_STOPS then return end
	local cs = stopsToColorSequence(self._stops)
	local color = sampleColorSequence(cs, time)
	table.insert(self._stops, {time = time, color = color})
	table.sort(self._stops, function(a,b) return a.time < b.time end)
	-- Finds the new stop after the sort by its time and its sampled colour.
	for i, s in ipairs(self._stops) do
		if math.abs(s.time - time) < 0.001 and s.color == color then
			self._selectedIndex = i; break
		end
	end
	self:_render()
	-- Wires any new frames; _stopDragWirer replaces earlier connections.
	if self._stopDragWirer then
		for i = 1, #self._stopFrames do self._stopDragWirer(i) end
	end
	self:_firePreview()
end

-- Shortest-arc hue lerp; hue wraps at 1.
local function lerpHue(h1, h2, alpha)
	local d = h2 - h1
	if d > 0.5 then d -= 1 elseif d < -0.5 then d += 1 end
	return (h1 + d * alpha) % 1
end

-- ColorSequence lerps RGB, which muddies distant hues (red to blue passes through grey-purple):
-- stops are added along the shorter hue arc, about one per 30 degrees, within MOST_STOPS.
function ColorGradientEditor:_smoothHues()
	local budget = ColorGradientEditor.MOST_STOPS - #self._stops
	if budget <= 0 then return end

	local plans = {}
	local total = 0
	for i = 1, #self._stops - 1 do
		local a, b = self._stops[i], self._stops[i + 1]
		local h1, s1, v1 = a.color:ToHSV()
		local h2, s2, v2 = b.color:ToHSV()
		-- Gray endpoints have no meaningful hue; RGB lerp is already correct there.
		if s1 > 0.05 and s2 > 0.05 and v1 > 0.05 and v2 > 0.05 and b.time - a.time > 1e-3 then
			local d = math.abs(h2 - h1)
			if d > 0.5 then d = 1 - d end
			local n = math.floor(d / (30 / 360))
			if n > 0 then
				table.insert(plans, { gap = i, count = n })
				total += n
			end
		end
	end
	if total == 0 then return end

	-- Over budget: each gap's share shrinks in proportion, then the largest give one up at a time.
	if total > budget then
		for _, p in ipairs(plans) do
			p.count = math.max(1, math.floor(p.count * budget / total))
		end
		total = 0
		for _, p in ipairs(plans) do total += p.count end
		while total > budget do
			table.sort(plans, function(x, y) return x.count > y.count end)
			plans[1].count -= 1
			total -= 1
		end
	end

	local newStops = {}
	for _, p in ipairs(plans) do
		if p.count > 0 then
			local a, b = self._stops[p.gap], self._stops[p.gap + 1]
			local h1, s1, v1 = a.color:ToHSV()
			local h2, s2, v2 = b.color:ToHSV()
			for k = 1, p.count do
				local alpha = k / (p.count + 1)
				table.insert(newStops, {
					time = a.time + (b.time - a.time) * alpha,
					color = Color3.fromHSV(lerpHue(h1, h2, alpha), s1 + (s2 - s1) * alpha, v1 + (v2 - v1) * alpha),
				})
			end
		end
	end
	for _, stop in ipairs(newStops) do table.insert(self._stops, stop) end
	table.sort(self._stops, function(x, y) return x.time < y.time end)

	self:_render()
	if self._stopDragWirer then
		for i = 1, #self._stopFrames do self._stopDragWirer(i) end
	end
	self:_firePreview()
end

-- A dragged inner stop to `time`: the list stays sorted as it passes its neighbours, the end
-- stops stay first and last. Returns the stop's index after; the caller draws and previews.
function ColorGradientEditor:_moveStop(index, time)
	local stops = self._stops
	local stop = stops[index]
	stop.time = math.clamp(time, 0, 1)
	while index > 2 and stop.time < stops[index - 1].time do
		stops[index], stops[index - 1] = stops[index - 1], stops[index]
		index -= 1
	end
	while index < #stops - 1 and stop.time > stops[index + 1].time do
		stops[index], stops[index + 1] = stops[index + 1], stops[index]
		index += 1
	end
	self._selectedIndex = index
	return index
end

-- A typed time for an inner stop, kept between its neighbours (a hair inside them where there is
-- room); an end stop's time stays. Returns whether the stop moved.
function ColorGradientEditor:_setStopTime(index, time)
	local stops = self._stops
	if not index or not time or index <= 1 or index >= #stops then
		return false
	end
	local low, high = stops[index - 1].time, stops[index + 1].time
	local margin = math.min(1e-4, (high - low) / 2)
	stops[index].time = math.clamp(time, low + margin, high - margin)
	self:_render()
	self:_firePreview()
	return true
end

-- Reverse: the sequence runs the other way; the selected stop stays selected.
function ColorGradientEditor:_reverse()
	local count = #self._stops
	for _, stop in ipairs(self._stops) do
		stop.time = 1 - stop.time
	end
	for index = 1, math.floor(count / 2) do
		self._stops[index], self._stops[count - index + 1] = self._stops[count - index + 1], self._stops[index]
	end
	if self._selectedIndex then
		self._selectedIndex = count - self._selectedIndex + 1
	end
	self:_render()
	self:_firePreview()
end

-- Even spacing: the stops keep their order and colours at equal steps of time.
function ColorGradientEditor:_evenSpacing()
	local count = #self._stops
	for index, stop in ipairs(self._stops) do
		stop.time = (index - 1) / (count - 1)
	end
	self:_render()
	self:_firePreview()
end

-- Reset to the start: the sequence the editor was opened with. The preview gets that sequence
-- itself, not a copy: a caller reads it as "each item back to its own" (Connectors).
function ColorGradientEditor:_reload()
	if self._originalCS then
		self:_loadCS(self._originalCS)
		self:_showLoaded()
		if self._state.onPreview then
			self._state.onPreview(self._originalCS)
		end
	end
end

function ColorGradientEditor:_deleteSelected()
	if not self._selectedIndex then return end
	if #self._stops <= 2 then return end
	-- The end stops cannot be deleted.
	if self._selectedIndex == 1 or self._selectedIndex == #self._stops then return end
	table.remove(self._stops, self._selectedIndex)
	self._selectedIndex = math.min(self._selectedIndex, #self._stops)
	self:_render()
	self:_firePreview()
end

function ColorGradientEditor:_loadCS(cs)
	self._stops = {}
	for _, kp in ipairs(cs.Keypoints) do
		table.insert(self._stops, {time = kp.Time, color = kp.Value})
	end
	self._selectedIndex = nil
end

-- options (the stops view; Classic ignores them): { items = what the sequence is for (its
-- colours fill "In this effect"), live = how many items show it live, anchor = the row that
-- opened it (the editor opens beside it, and reads its section's name), title = the name the view
-- shows, where it differs from propertyName }.
function ColorGradientEditor:Open(colorSequence, propertyName, onApply, onPreview, position, options)
	self._state.propName = propertyName or ""
	self._state.onApply = onApply
	self._state.onPreview = onPreview
	self._originalCS = colorSequence
	self._closing = false

	self:_loadCS(colorSequence)
	if self._view then
		self._panel.Visible = true
		self._view.open(self._state.propName, options, position)
		return
	end
	self._title.Text = "Color - " .. self._state.propName

	-- Opens beside the element that asked for it, until the user has put the panel somewhere:
	-- from then on it opens where it was left.
	if position and not self._placedByHand then
		self._panel.Position = position
	end

	self._panel.Size = UDim2.new(0, PANEL_W, 0, PANEL_H)
	self._panel.Visible = true
	self:_showLoaded()
end

-- What every way of closing shares: the view's menu and code, or Classic's code popup and ghost.
function ColorGradientEditor:_hideParts()
	if self._view then
		self._view.close()
		return
	end
	if self._codePopup then self._codePopup.Visible = false end
	self._ghost.Visible = false
end

function ColorGradientEditor:_rawClose()
	self._panel.Visible = false
	self:_hideParts()
	self._state.onApply = nil
	self._state.onPreview = nil
	self._closing = false
	self._selectedIndex = nil
	-- A close mid-drag must not leave _dragging set for the next Open.
	self._dragging = false
	self._dragIndex = nil
	-- OnCancel cleared first, so the picker's revert cannot undo the Apply.
	if self._pickerOpen and self._colorPicker then
		self._colorPicker:SetOnCancel(nil)
		self._colorPicker:Close()
		self._pickerOpen = false
	end
end

function ColorGradientEditor:Close()
	if self._closing then return end
	self._closing = true
	-- The preview goes back to the original.
	if self._state.onPreview and self._originalCS then
		self._state.onPreview(self._originalCS)
	end
	self._originalCS = nil
	self._state.onApply = nil; self._state.onPreview = nil

	self._panel.Visible = false
	self._closing = false
	self._selectedIndex = nil
	self:_hideParts()
	-- A ColorPicker opened for a stop closes too, as on Apply.
	if self._pickerOpen and self._colorPicker then
		self._colorPicker:SetOnCancel(nil)
		self._colorPicker:Close()
		self._pickerOpen = false
	end
	-- As in _rawClose: no drag state carries into the next Open.
	self._dragging = false
	self._dragIndex = nil
end

function ColorGradientEditor:IsOpen() return self._panel.Visible and not self._closing end
function ColorGradientEditor:GetPanel() return self._panel end

-- Modules/PanelPersistence saves the panel's place only while this is true, sets it when it
-- restores a saved place and clears it on Reset Layout.
function ColorGradientEditor:IsPlacedByHand()
	return self._placedByHand
end

function ColorGradientEditor:SetPlacedByHand(placed)
	self._placedByHand = placed == true
end

-- PanelPersistence: the stops view is resized by hand and keeps its width; Classic's is fixed.
function ColorGradientEditor:ResizesByHand()
	return self._view ~= nil
end

function ColorGradientEditor:RefreshTheme()
	-- The stops view is built from the plugin's panel pieces: the theme's walk repaints it.
	if self._view then
		return
	end
	local T = self._T
	self._panel.BackgroundColor3 = T.PanelBg
	local panelStroke = self._panel:FindFirstChildOfClass("UIStroke")
	if panelStroke then panelStroke.Color = T.Border; panelStroke.Transparency = T.BorderAlpha end
	local panelCorner = self._panel:FindFirstChildOfClass("UICorner")
	if panelCorner then panelCorner.CornerRadius = T.BigCorner end
	self._title.TextColor3 = T.Gold; self._title.Font = T.Font
	self._closeBtn.TextColor3 = T.DarkGold; self._closeBtn.Font = T.Font
	local barStroke = self._barFrame:FindFirstChildOfClass("UIStroke")
	if barStroke then barStroke.Color = T.Border; barStroke.Transparency = T.BorderAlpha end
	self._ghost.TextColor3 = T.DarkGold
	self._timeInput.BackgroundColor3 = T.BlobBg; self._timeInput.BackgroundTransparency = T.BlobAlpha
	self._timeInput.TextColor3 = T.BrightGold; self._timeInput.Font = T.Font
	self._deleteBtn.BackgroundColor3 = T.BlobBg; self._deleteBtn.BackgroundTransparency = T.BlobAlpha
	self._deleteBtn.Font = T.Font
	local delStroke = self._deleteBtn:FindFirstChildOfClass("UIStroke")
	if delStroke then delStroke.Color = T.Border; delStroke.Transparency = T.BorderAlpha end
	for _, btn in ipairs({self._invertBtn, self._huesBtn, self._reloadBtn, self._cancelBtn, self._applyBtn, self._codeBtn, self._copyBtn, self._pasteBtn}) do
		btn.BackgroundColor3 = T.BlobBg; btn.BackgroundTransparency = T.BlobAlpha; btn.Font = T.Font
		local s = btn:FindFirstChildOfClass("UIStroke")
		if s then s.Color = T.Border; s.Transparency = T.BorderAlpha end
	end
	-- The lines above write the theme font; the mode's own text fonts and sizes go back on.
	TypeScale.reapply(self._panel)
	if self._panel.Visible then self:_render() end
end

function ColorGradientEditor:Destroy()
	for _, c in ipairs(self._conns) do c:Disconnect() end
	self._conns = {}
	if self._pickerOpen and self._colorPicker then
		self._colorPicker:Close()
	end
	if self._view then
		self._view.destroy()
	elseif self._panel then
		self._panel:Destroy()
	end
end

require(script.CodeIO)(ColorGradientEditor)

return ColorGradientEditor
